The provided text describes a standard cybersecurity practice known as the principle of least privilege. By disabling administrator privileges for standard user accounts, the company significantly reduces the attack surface, preventing malware from gaining high-level system access and stopping users from inadvertently or maliciously altering critical system configurations. The requirement for a formal request process ensures that all changes are tracked, authorized, and reviewed, which supports accountability and auditability. Therefore, the content is compliant with standard cybersecurity policies.

The first three months of the year are January, February, and March.
